habitat: Pairs in woodland, riparian forest, valley bush and bushveld.
summary: A common summer resident with two colour morphs. One has black upper parts, white underparts and a crest. The other is black except for a white wing-bar. The call is a shrill kleeuw, pewp-pewp. It parasitises bulbuls and other small birds. Months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Black Cuckoo is entirely black and can show faint barring below. The black Jacobin morph has a white wing-bar.
Levaillant’s Cuckoo is larger than the white Jacobin morph and is heavily streaked on the throat and breast.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^14=16384 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 8192–32768.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

wings.pattern: White wing-bar. This separates it from Black Cuckoo.

viewNotes.note: Pied morph: black above, white below, with a crest. The black morph is black except for a white wing-bar.
Pied morph: white underparts and a crest. Black morph: black throat and breast, with the white mark in the wing.
Black upper parts and a crest. The black morph shows the white wing-bar from behind.
The white wing-bar is the flight mark given for the black morph. The pied upperwing was not described beyond black.
Pied morph white below. Black morph black below.

calls.description: A shrill, flute-like kleeuw, pewp-pewp, kleeuw, pewp-pewp. Newman does not separate the sexes. Grade A call from Kruger, near Sabie Park. The filename is jacob-cuckoo-call.
